title: Repetitive low-level blast exposure and brain health: State-of-the-science and clinical priorities in 2026
title_zh: 低水平爆炸波反复暴露与脑健康：2026年的科学现状与临床优先事项
abstract: Low-level blast (LLB) exposures generated by weapons systems and explosives use are now recognized as an occupational hazard for many military and law-enforcement communities. Although individual exposures often fall below thresholds for clinically diagnosable concussion, accumulating data from human and animal studies suggest that repetitive LLB can produce subtle but durable changes in neurobehavioral function, neuroimaging markers, and blood- and CSF-based biomarkers, as well as cardiovascular and neurovascular health. At the same time, the field remains fragmented, with heterogeneous exposure metrics, characterized by non-standardized exposure quantification methods, variable outcome measures, and inconsistent longitudinal follow-up intervals. This state-of-the-science review synthesizes current evidence on LLB with a deliberate emphasis on clinical aspects that matter to Servicemembers, Veterans, and clinicians focusing on posttraumatic outcomes (e.g., psychological, cognitive, physical), reduction of risk of neurodegenerative disease, and practical pathways for exposure prevention and mitigation. We first describe contemporary definitions and patterns of LLB exposure across operational communities, followed by a critical appraisal of epidemiological studies linking LLB to symptoms, functional outcomes, and health-care utilization. We then summarize converging evidence for neurodegenerative and neurovascular risks, integrate mechanistic insights from neuroimaging, neuropathology, and animal models, and highlight emerging biomarker and computational approaches. Finally, we outline pragmatic strategies for exposure assessment, screening, and follow-up in clinical settings and identify high-priority research and policy directions. Rather than asking whether LLB is "safe" or "unsafe" in absolute terms, we focus on vulnerability and context as a roadmap for scientific and clinical development while balancing mission requirements with long-term brain health.
abstract_zh: 低水平爆炸波（LLB）暴露是由武器系统和爆炸物使用产生的，现已被认定为许多军队和执法社区的职业危害。虽然单次暴露往往低于临床可诊断的脑震荡阈值，但来自人类和动物研究的累积数据表明，重复的LLB可导致神经行为功能、神经影像标志以及血液和脑脊液生物标志物的细微但持久变化，并影响心血管和神经血管健康。与此同时，该领域仍然碎片化，暴露指标异质，缺乏标准化的暴露量化方法，结果测量多样，纵向随访间隔不一致。本综述聚焦于对军人、退伍军人和关注创伤后结果（如心理、认知、身体）的临床医生重要的临床方面，综合当前关于LLB的证据，并强调降低神经退行性疾病风险和实际的暴露预防与缓解路径。我们首先描述了在作战社区中LLB暴露的当代定义和模式，然后对将LLB与症状、功能结果和医疗利用相关联的流行病学研究进行批判性评估。随后，我们总结了关于神经退行性和神经血管风险的共识证据，整合了神经影像、神经病理学和动物模型的机制洞见，并突出新兴的生物标志物和计算方法。最后，我们概述了在临床环境中进行暴露评估、筛查和随访的实用策略，并确定了高优先级的研究和政策方向。我们不再以绝对意义上问LLB是“安全”还是“不安全”，而是关注易感性和情境，作为科学和临床发展的路线图，同时平衡任务需求与长期脑健康。
